attendance_levels: Two or three times a month
formulas: X = [age basis (4 columns, looked up by integer age), female, educ_secondary, educ_higher, town_small, town_mid, city, metropolis, relig, relig2, ses, ses2] minus centres
relig = (attendance level 1-6 minus relig_centre) / relig_scale; relig2 = relig^2 before centring; ses = ses_z for the chosen quintile; ses2 = ses^2 before centring
age_c = (age - age_mean) / age_sd; big_c = (residence level >= 4) - bigcity_mean
XI = [age_c*educ_secondary, age_c*educ_higher, age_c*relig, big_c*educ_secondary, big_c*educ_higher, female*age_c], with the centred educ, relig and female columns of X
eta_k = coef[k][0] + sum(X * coef[k][1..P]) + sum(XI * coef[k][P+1..P+Q]); probabilities = softmax(0, eta_1..eta_K), first entry is not voting

support.note: Kernel-weighted counts of observed respondents like the person on each pair of characteristics; the calculator uses the smallest of the four.

impossible.message: A degree takes until at least 21; nobody in the survey is in this position.

warn.message: A bachelor's degree is possible at this age, but few respondents are in this position.

support_messages.stop: Too few respondents like this person in this election for a reliable estimate.
support_messages.warn: Few respondents like this person in this election: read the interval, not the point estimate.

items: Role of the Church in the state
Preferred state: tradition or progress (% tradition)

attitudes.formula: eta = sum((X, XI) * beta[d]); P(position <= k) = 1 / (1 + exp(-(cut[d][k] - eta))), k = 0..9; probability of position k = P(<= k) - P(<= k-1), with P(<= -1) = 0 and P(<= 10) = 1
attitudes.note: Positions are rounded to 0-10 with 10 the right or conservative pole. Economic and socio-cultural positions are the mean of the survey's items on that issue, which differ between elections, so they are comparable between people in one election and not between elections.
